reply.content:
Yes. **Opioid litigation was the most financially significant ongoing legal matter:** CVS reported a 2022 judgment of $651 million against three pharmacy defendants—which it was appealing—and agreed to multiyear settlements with state and tribal plaintiffs. The filing says private opioid litigation would continue, and CVS recorded $5.8 billion in opioid-related charges in 2022.

Other ongoing matters included lawsuits and government investigations into PBM drug pricing and rebates, litigation over pharmacy “usual and customary” pricing, and Medicare risk-adjustment audits and investigations. Certain shareholder and ERISA cases concerning the long-term-care business also remained in litigation, including an appeal. **CVS stated that it could not predict the outcomes of many proceedings; it did not claim all were likely to have a material adverse effect.**

*Justification:* The opioid judgment, settlements, continuing claims and related charges are described on pp. 174–175; PBM and pricing matters on pp. 173–174; Medicare audits on pp. 175–176; and shareholder/ERISA proceedings on p. 177.
